title: How to start investing with fractional shares in the US
description: Why dollar-based investing is the greatest innovation for retail investors.
content:
In the old days (pre-2019), if you wanted to buy Amazon stock, you needed $3,000 for a single share. If you had $500 to invest, you simply couldn't buy it. You were priced out of the best companies. The invention of **Fractional Shares** changed the game. Now, you can buy $1 of Amazon, $5 of Berkshire Hathaway, or $10 of a Vanguard ETF. This 'Dollar-Based Investing' democratizes wealth, allowing you to invest every single penny of your paycheck without leaving cash idle waiting to afford a 'whole' share.

Key Takeaways

  • Zero Cash Drag: You don't have to wait until you have $400 to buy an ETF trading at $400. You invest your $50 immediately.
  • Exact Budgeting: You can allocate your portfolio by percentage (e.g., 50% VTI, 50% VXUS) precisely, regardless of share price.
  • Diversification for $100: You can build a portfolio of 50 different stocks with just $100 total capital.
  • DRIP Efficiency: Dividend Reinvestment Plans (DRIP) use fractional shares to reinvest dividends instantly, compounding your growth.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Fractional shares are a custodial feature. The stock market technically trades in whole shares, but your broker (Fidelity/Robinhood) buys the whole share and assigns 0.1 of it to you in their ledger. This means you must stick with major, trustworthy US brokers to ensure proper accounting.

How to Place a Fractional Trade

The process is slightly different than a traditional trade.

Step 1: Choose a Capable Broker

Not all brokers support this.

  • Fidelity: Supports fractional Stocks AND ETFs. (Best).
  • Robinhood: Supports Stocks and ETFs.
  • Schwab: Supports S&P 500 Stocks only (No ETFs). (Limited).
  • Vanguard: Does NOT support fractional ETF purchases (except via DRIP).

Step 2: The 'Dollar' Order

When you click 'Buy', switch the order type from 'Shares' to 'Dollars'.

Input: "Buy $100 of VTI".

Result: If VTI is $250, you will own 0.40 shares. You get 40% of the dividends and 40% of the growth.

Step 3: Dividends

If the stock pays a $1.00 dividend per share, and you own 0.40 shares, you receive $0.40. It scales perfectly.

Strategies Unlocked by Fractions

  1. Dollar Cost Averaging: You can automate a transfer of exactly $100/week from your bank to buy exactly $100 of stock. No math required.
  2. Custom Indexing: You can build your own 'Tech ETF' by buying $10 each of Apple, Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia. No management fees.
  3. Gift Investing: You can give a child $50 of Disney stock. It is a powerful educational tool.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are fractional shares real ownership?

Yes. You have voting rights (pro-rated) and receive dividends. If you transfer brokers, they might liquidate the fraction (sell it for cash) and transfer only the whole shares.

Are there extra fees?

No. At major brokers, fractional trades are $0 commission, just like whole share trades.

Can I limit order fractions?

Usually no. Most fractional trades are 'Market Orders' executed at the current price. This is fine for long-term investors but bad for day traders.
